## Solution

The cone $CX$ is contractible, so
$$H_n(CX) = 0 \text{ for } n \geq 1, \qquad H_0(CX) \cong \mathbb{Z}.$$

Since $X$ has five path components,
$$H_0(X) \cong \mathbb{Z}^5, \qquad H_n(X) = 0 \text{ for } n \geq 1 \text{ (assumed for the reduced part of the argument; only } H_0 \text{ is needed)}.$$

Consider the long exact sequence of the pair $(CX, X)$:
$$\cdots \to H_1(CX) \to H_1(CX, X) \to \widetilde{H}_0(X) \to \widetilde{H}_0(CX) \to \cdots$$

Using reduced homology (which is cleaner here, since $CX$ is contractible so $\widetilde{H}_*(CX) = 0$), the long exact sequence gives:
$$0 = H_1(CX) \to H_1(CX, X) \to \widetilde{H}_0(X) \to \widetilde{H}_0(CX) = 0.$$

By exactness:
- The map $H_1(CX, X) \to \widetilde{H}_0(X)$ is **injective** (its kernel equals the image of $H_1(CX) = 0$).
- The map $\widetilde{H}_0(X) \to \widetilde{H}_0(CX) = 0$ is the zero map, so the image of $H_1(CX, X) \to \widetilde{H}_0(X)$ equals $\ker(\widetilde{H}_0(X) \to 0) = \widetilde{H}_0(X)$, i.e., the map is **surjective**.

Therefore
$$H_1(CX, X) \cong \widetilde{H}_0(X).$$

Now $X$ has five path components, so
$$\widetilde{H}_0(X) \cong \mathbb{Z}^{5-1} = \mathbb{Z}^4.$$

**Equivalently, via unreduced homology:** the relevant portion of the long exact sequence is
$$0 = H_1(CX) \to H_1(CX, X) \xrightarrow{\;\partial\;} H_0(X) \cong \mathbb{Z}^5 \xrightarrow{\;i_*\;} H_0(CX) \cong \mathbb{Z} \to H_0(CX, X) \to 0.$$
The inclusion-induced map $i_* : \mathbb{Z}^5 \to \mathbb{Z}$ sends each of the five component-generators to the single generator of $H_0(CX) \cong \mathbb{Z}$, i.e. it is the summation map $(a_1,\dots,a_5) \mapsto a_1 + \cdots + a_5$, which is surjective with kernel $\cong \mathbb{Z}^4$. Exactness gives
$$H_1(CX, X) \cong \ker(i_*) \cong \mathbb{Z}^4.$$

### Answer

$$\boxed{H_1(CX, X) \cong \mathbb{Z}^4.}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
